conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice; complex Hilbert inner products are linear in the first argument; natural-number basis indices start at zero.
L² vectors are almost-everywhere classes. Polynomial-Gaussian classes use their unique smooth representatives. Set g₋₁=0; [a,a†]=aa†−a†a=I on the polynomial-Gaussian space.
The Fourier transform has kernel exp(−2πiξy). Polynomial moments in the completeness criterion use the bilinear integral ∫fqg₀, without conjugating q.

m, ω and ℏ are positive real parameters; ℓ=√(ℏ/(mω)). The oscillator domain is the stated squared-eigenvalue coefficient domain. Its differential identity holds pointwise on the core and bilinearly against compactly supported smooth tests on the full operator domain; no maximal differential-domain identification is asserted.
The closed ladder operators have the displayed weighted coefficient domains. Both product domains equal D(N); the closed-operator commutator is asserted only on D(N).
Q=Mₓ and P=F₂* M₂πℏξ F₂ on their maximal multiplier domains. U(t) has phases exp(−iω(n+1/2)t). Variance means the squared norm of the centered operator applied to the unit vector.
d≥1; completed tensor products are left-associated. Multi-indices are enumerated by increasing total degree, then lexicographically. Nonnegative indexed sums also mean suprema of finite subsums.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, for a complete orthonormal sequence in a complex Hilbert space and real λₙ, the finite-support diagonal operator S has S*=A, A*=A and closure S=A, where D(A)={x:Σλₙ²|⟨x,eₙ⟩|²<∞}. A is its unique self-adjoint extension; finite truncations converge in graph norm.

Under Countable Choice, if f∈L²(R) and ∫fqg₀=0 for every complex polynomial q, then f=0 almost everywhere. The Hermite family is a complete orthonormal family of L²(R), with its coefficient expansion and Parseval identity, and P is dense.

Under Countable Choice, on P={pg₀:p∈C[y]}, g₀=π⁻¹/⁴exp(−y²/2) is a unit vector, a=(Y+∂y)/√2 and a†=(Y−∂y)/√2 satisfy the adjoint pairings and [a,a†]=I; the defined gₙ satisfy the ladder identities and gₙ=Hₙg₀/√(2ⁿn!), with the stated Rodrigues and recurrence formulas.

Under Countable Choice, the self-adjoint diagonal operator has σ(A)=closure{λₙ}. A scalar λ is in the resolvent exactly when d=infₙ|λ−λₙ|>0; its resolvent is the coefficient multiplier (λ−λₙ)⁻¹ and has norm d⁻¹. Closure points not equal to any λₙ are approximate eigenvalues but not eigenvalues.

Under Countable Choice and m,ω,ℏ>0, Df(x)=ℓ⁻¹/²f(x/ℓ) is unitary. Hosc=(ℏω/2)DAD⁻¹ is self-adjoint with complete eigenbasis ψₙ=Dgₙ, eigenvalues ℏω(n+1/2), the displayed coefficient domain and polynomial-Gaussian graph core. It equals the oscillator differential expression on that core and satisfies the stated weak identity on its full domain.

Under Countable Choice, the displayed weighted shifts a and a† are closed and mutually adjoint, with kernels Ce₀ and {0}. D(aa†)=D(a†a)=D(N), a†a=N and aa†=N+I there. N is self-adjoint with spectrum N; for the Hermite family the shifts are exactly the closures of the polynomial-Gaussian ladder operators.

Under Countable Choice, ψz=exp(−|z|²/2)Σzⁿgₙ/√n! converges to a unit vector in every D(Nᵏ), satisfies aψz=zψz, has overlap exp(−(|z|²+|w|²)/2+z conjugate(w)), and has number mean |z|² and creation norm squared |z|²+1.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.2 writes the norm of a sum indexed by 'm≤M<N' equal to Σ_{M<m≤N} λ_m²|⟨x,e_m⟩|². The left-hand summation range does not describe the tail on the right. The intended range M<m≤N is immediate, and the surrounding square-summability argument is sound, but the displayed identity needs correction.

alerts.finding: The summary of this proposition on library/non-relativistic-quantum-mechanics-mathematics/qm-math-orbital-and-spin.md says that the matrices 'J_z e_m=me_m' and 'J_± e_m=√((s∓m)(s±m+1)) e_{m±1}' 'are self-adjoint'. This is false for J_± when s>0: at s=1/2, J_+ is the nonzero upper-triangular raising matrix and its adjoint is J_−. The proposition itself correctly states in clause (a) that J_x,J_y,J_z are self-adjoint and J_+*=J_−. The defect is in the owning page's summary, not the proposition's Statement.

seams_checked.note: The multidimensional theorem uses the actual completed tensor construction, bounded tensor maps and Euclidean L² product unitary. It specifies the recursive maps and uses Countable Choice; it does not infer unbounded tensor-domain identities from bounded-map results.
The interval-spectrum consumer uses the diagonal lemma for the sine basis; differential-domain equality and sine completeness are separately supplied by the interval results.

The model and its spectral/coherent consumers preserve positivity, scaled coefficient domains, ladder product domains and weak/core differential scope. Physical observable and outcome-law interpretations are supplied separately.
The Gaussian and ladder examples faithfully use the scaling and closed-ladder results. The page distinguishes operator norms and conditional outcome laws from measurements.
The thermal-occupation consumer applies the diagonal lemma to a supplied countable occupation basis with the exact squared-weight domain and graph core.
The sphere diagonal-domain and harmonic-polynomial consumers preserve the diagonal and isotropic product-basis statements. The separate spin-summary defect is recorded in alerts.
Dirichlet, compact-resolvent and twisted-periodic consumers use real diagonal weights and coefficient domains; interval differential realizations require their own additional arguments.
The separated-box example uses the diagonal lemma and coefficient comparison for the two-dimensional eigenspace at 5π²/L².
The dipole-domain theorem's oscillator comparison uses the scaled Hermite recurrence, with the lowering term omitted at n=0 or the zero-vector convention.

Driven-oscillator consumers use the exact diagonal domain, finite Hermite graph core and weighted ladder actions. Extensions to position/momentum actions and Weyl-domain invariance are treated as further local arguments.

The countable-mode product theorem uses the diagonal lemma on its occupation basis; proof step 3.1 explicitly enumerates the countably infinite multiset index set. Trace-class conclusions use separate trace suppliers.
